answer: Proof-of-location can resist Sybil attacks: a registry pings each agent from scattered vantage points and accepts only responses matching a distinct, stable network position. Ten claimed agents on a karst ridge whose terrace lookouts all echo down one ferrous cable show identical jitter, so the registry merges them into one operator; every fake identity then needs its own real endpoint and bandwidth bill, making the cost linear while the payout stays shared.
